Description: List local businesses in a target niche/area with no site, an outdated site, or a site that fails mobile/speed checks; record name, contact, source, current URL
Why necessary: A pipeline of qualified leads is the only reliable source of projects
Possible risks: Scraping personal data without basis; wasted time on poor-fit niches
Common mistakes: Listing everyone instead of a niche; no source tracking

Description: Quick audit of prospect's site, Google Business Profile, socials: mobile view, speed, HTTPS, broken contact info; 3–5 concrete findings
Why necessary: Gives a specific, credible reason to talk
Possible risks: Over-investing in leads that never reply

Task: Log lead with source and status
Description: Create lead record: business, contact person, phone/email, source, date, next action, status
Why necessary: Lead source data shows which channels pay off; prevents double contact
Common mistakes: Keeping leads only in personal WhatsApp
If skipped: Partners contact same lead twice; lost revenue

Description: Ask past clients, CAs, printers, photographers, marketers for referrals; track referrer
Why necessary: Referrals convert better and cost less

Description: Draft first message referencing audit findings and a clear next step (15-min call)
Why necessary: Personalised, specific outreach gets replies; generic spam damages reputation
Possible risks: Spam complaints; WhatsApp account restriction for bulk messaging
Common mistakes: Copy-paste bulk messages; no call to action

Description: Call/visit/message; record date, channel, who, outcome, next step
Why necessary: Creates the audit trail for who sourced the client
Possible risks: Disputes between partners about who brought the client

Description: Up to 2–3 spaced follow-ups with added value (example, audit point); stop after no response
Why necessary: Most deals need follow-up; a cap prevents harassment

Description: Send 2–3 relevant samples with outcome, scope and price band
15–30 min call covering need, decision-maker, budget range, timeline, existing assets
Why necessary: Filters out bad-fit and non-paying clients early
Common mistakes: Skipping budget question; promising features on call

Description: Decide proceed or decline using checklist: budget fit, timeline realism, legal business, red flags; record reason
Possible risks: Taking every project, including toxic ones

Description: Present approach, process, timeline, samples; explain payment terms and ownership model upfront
Why necessary: Sets expectations before numbers are discussed

Description: Negotiate by adjusting scope, not just price; record every concession in writing
Why necessary: Discounts without scope change erode margin

Description: Check GSTIN (if B2B), business legitimacy, prohibited content/activities, previous vendor disputes
Common mistakes: Ignoring red flags due to urgency

Description: Send structured questionnaire (see Part 5) via form/doc with deadline
Why necessary: Collects facts before the call; reduces call time

Description: 60–90 min structured meeting walking through goals, pages, features, content, accounts, timeline, budget
Common mistakes: Letting client design the solution on the call

Description: Send written summary of what was understood, open questions, and next steps within 24–48 h
Why necessary: Creates written record client can correct

Task: Identify decision-maker and single point of contact
Description: Record who approves design, content, payments; one SPOC for feedback
Why necessary: Prevents conflicting feedback from multiple people
Possible risks: Late veto by an unseen owner

Description: Identify current domain registrar and registrant, hosting, email provider, DNS host, analytics, GBP, socials, and who holds logins
Why necessary: Ownership problems block launch; must be found early
Possible risks: Domain registered in a former vendor's name

Description: Agree 2–4 measurable goals (e.g., enquiries/month, calls, bookings) and how they will be measured
Why necessary: Guides design priorities and later proves value
Possible risks: Vague goals lead to subjective acceptance

Description: List every page with purpose and priority; mark template vs unique pages
Why necessary: Page count drives price and timeline
Common mistakes: Not distinguishing templated vs unique pages

Description: List features (forms, booking, blog, gallery, payments, languages) marked Must/Should/Could/Won't
Why necessary: Separates core scope from optional add-ons

Description: For every page/section: who writes text, supplies images, approves, and by when
Why necessary: Content delays are the most common cause of late projects

Description: List every external service (maps, payments, booking, CRM, email), who creates the account, costs, and API limits
Why necessary: Third-party accounts must be in client's name and ready before build

Description: Agree supported browsers/devices, accessibility target, performance targets, languages, hosting region, uptime expectations
Why necessary: These drive testing effort and cost
Possible risks: Client assumes IE-era or all devices
If skipped: Endless 'it looks wrong on my phone' disputes

Description: Client confirms requirements document in writing (e-sign or email 'approved')
Why necessary: Baseline for all later change requests

Description: Enumerate exactly what is delivered: pages, templates, features, integrations, content work, rounds, training, warranty days
Why necessary: Clear inclusions prevent 'I thought that was included'

Description: List what is NOT included (copywriting, logo, photos, paid ads, content entry beyond X pages, third-party fees) and assumptions (content supplied by date, one SPOC)
Why necessary: Exclusions carry as much weight as inclusions

Description: Specify number of rounds per stage, what a round is (one consolidated list), and what counts as a change request
Why necessary: Unlimited revisions are the top profit killer
Possible risks: Piecemeal feedback treated as one round

Task: Define client responsibilities and feedback SLAs
Description: Client duties: content, approvals within N working days, account creation, payments; effect of delay on timeline
Why necessary: Client delays must shift deadlines, not your margins

Description: Milestones (design, build, UAT, launch) with measurable acceptance tests and deemed-acceptance rule
Estimate each task from the task library with low/high range, add risk buffer (10–25%)
Convert effort to price; add third-party costs (pass-through or client-paid), GST if registered, contingency; set payment split
Proposal with problem, solution, scope summary, timeline, price, payment schedule, ownership model, validity date
Itemised quotation with GSTIN/SAC and tax lines if registered, validity, terms reference
Why necessary: Some clients need a formal quote for internal approval/accounting

Description: Walk client through proposal; answer questions; log objections
Update scope/price after negotiation; increment version; mark superseded
Why necessary: Only one current version should exist

Description: Start from lawyer-reviewed master services agreement; select project schedule; do not edit core clauses ad hoc
Why necessary: Consistent, reviewed terms reduce legal risk
Possible risks: Using internet templates with foreign law
Common mistakes: Changing clauses per client without review

Description: Attach scope, milestones, payment schedule, revision policy, timeline, client duties as a schedule to the contract
Why necessary: Keeps legal terms stable and project details specific

Description: Confirm clause: what is assigned (in writing, with duration/territory), what is licensed (pre-existing code, libraries, templates), third-party licences, portfolio rights
Why necessary: Indian copyright assignment has statutory formalities; silence creates default rules
Possible risks: Client assumes payment = ownership of everything incl. your reusable code

Description: Add confidentiality; if you will access/process personal data (form leads, customers), add processor-style terms: purpose, security, deletion, breach notice
Why necessary: DPDP Act expects fiduciaries to use processors under a valid contract
Possible risks: Handling client customer data without terms

Description: Both parties sign (e-sign/wet); store final PDF; record date, version, signatories and authority
Why necessary: A signed contract is the core evidence in any dispute

Description: Check applicable state stamp duty for the agreement type/value; pay via e-stamp if required
Why necessary: Unstamped instruments can be inadmissible in evidence until duty and penalty are paid
Common mistakes: Assuming email contracts never need stamping

Description: Issue invoice for advance (e.g., 30–50%) with correct GST details if registered
Why necessary: Advance funds work and filters non-serious clients

Description: Match bank credit to invoice; issue receipt/acknowledgement; record TDS if deducted
Why necessary: Work starts only on confirmed funds
Common mistakes: Trusting screenshots instead of bank credit

Description: Invoice each milestone on acceptance or deemed acceptance
Record TDS deducted by client, check it appears in Form 26AS/AIS, request TDS certificate
Why necessary: You can only claim credit for TDS that is deposited and reported

Description: Polite reminders at due date, +7, +14 days; escalate per contract; log each
Why necessary: Late payment is common; a process removes awkwardness

Description: Record every third-party purchase (theme, plugin, stock image, domain) with bill, payer, reimbursable flag
Why necessary: Expenses affect profit split and client billing

Task: Create project record and folder structure
Description: Create project in tracking app and shared drive with standard folders (01-Contract, 02-Brief, 03-Content, 04-Design, 05-Dev, 06-QA, 07-Launch, 08-Handover, 09-Finance)
Why necessary: Standard structure makes evidence findable and handover easy

Description: Import default tasks from library, delete irrelevant ones, set owners, due dates, milestones
Why necessary: Visible plan avoids forgotten work and supports contribution tracking

Task: Set up client communication channel and rules
Description: Choose official channels (email for decisions, WhatsApp group for quick coordination), response times, working hours, SPOC
Why necessary: Decisions buried in chats cause disputes
Common mistakes: Taking approvals over voice calls only

Description: Create repo (ideally in a business-owned organization or client-owned org), branch protection, README stub, .gitignore excluding secrets
Why necessary: Version control is evidence and safety net
Possible risks: Repo in personal account hard to transfer

Task: Set up dev and staging environments
Description: Local dev setup, password-protected or noindex staging URL for client review
Why necessary: Client reviews must not be indexed or public
Possible risks: Staging indexed by Google; client data on public staging

Description: Create shared vault (password manager) for project credentials with item naming convention
Why necessary: Credentials must never live in chats or docs

Description: Walk through plan, timeline, responsibilities, content deadlines, communication rules, next steps; send notes

Task: Internal task assignment and point pre-estimate
Description: Partners agree owners and default points for each task before work starts; lock the plan
Why necessary: Pre-agreement is the strongest defence against later point disputes
Evidence of completion: App lock record with both confirmations

Description: Short written update: done, next, blockers, decisions needed, client actions pending
Why necessary: Keeps client informed and documents delays

Description: Send invite with agenda, goal, attendees, materials
Notes within 24 h: decisions, actions with owner and due date, open questions; client asked to correct
Why necessary: Written record of what was decided

Description: Maintain log of decisions: date, decision, who approved, source link
Why necessary: Single source of truth for scope decisions

Description: Handle serious issues (delays, payment, conflict) by call plus written summary with options
Understand client's services, customer questions, regulatory/professional display norms to confirm with client
Define 2–3 audience types, their key questions, devices, languages
Possible risks: Designing for the client's taste only

Description: Find search terms (service + locality), questions, and competitor terms; map to pages
Decide stack (static, CMS, framework, hosting) with reasons: client skills, budget, maintenance, hosting costs
Possible risks: Choosing trendy tools client can't maintain

Description: List legal pages/disclosures the client must provide (privacy notice, terms, refund policy for e-commerce, grievance contact) and flag for client's lawyer
Why necessary: Legal text is the client's responsibility but must be planned
Possible risks: Developer drafting legal text as advice

Description: Choose 3–5 direct/local competitors and 1–2 aspirational ones with client
Review structure, messaging, CTAs, trust signals, pricing display, mobile experience; screenshots
Note titles, key pages, GBP presence, reviews volume
Obtain logo (vector SVG/AI/PDF), colours, fonts, brand guide, photo library
Confirm client owns logo, has licences for fonts/photos they supply; record licence files
Why necessary: You may be publishing infringing material
Possible risks: Font licences not covering web use

Description: Define palette, type pairing, logo usage if client has none
Logo concepts, refinement, final files and copyright assignment
Why necessary: Logo is a separate creative deliverable

Description: Per page list of required text, images, videos, documents with due dates and format specs
Receive files in organised folder; reject WhatsApp-compressed images where quality matters
Mark each page item: pending/received/edited/approved
Confirm source/licence for each image; photos of identifiable people/customers have consent; stock licence saved
Why necessary: Publishing unlicensed or non-consented images creates liability

Description: Crop, resize, compress, convert (WebP/AVIF), rename descriptively, write alt text drafts

Task: Chase missing content and record delays
Description: Remind client per plan; log delay days; notify timeline impact in writing
Write headline, value proposition, sections, CTAs based on research
Why necessary: Homepage drives first impression and conversion

Description: Write service/about/contact/FAQ copy
Common mistakes: Pricing per project not per page

Description: Integrate target keywords naturally in headings, intro, titles; avoid stuffing
Button labels, form hints, error messages, success messages, empty states
Proofread all copy; client approves final text in writing
Why necessary: Client is responsible for factual accuracy of their content

Description: Translate content to additional language(s) by qualified translator; client review
Map flows for primary tasks (call, enquire, book, buy) from entry to success
Define navigation labels, hierarchy, footer links, URL structure
For each template define section order and priority
Place calls, WhatsApp, forms, booking CTAs; define tracking events
Grey-box wireframes, mobile-first, for each unique template
Why necessary: Cheap to change; locks structure before visuals

Description: Walkthrough; collect consolidated feedback
Apply one consolidated round; record approval
1–2 visual directions (colour, type, imagery, UI style)
Desktop and mobile designs of homepage with real content
Designs for each unique template (service, about, contact, blog list/post, product) desktop+mobile
Common mistakes: Designing every page instead of templates

Description: Hover, focus, active, disabled, loading, error, success, empty states for components
Check contrast (4.5:1 text), target sizes (24px min), focus visibility, not relying on colour alone
Export assets, document spacing, breakpoints, component names, interactions
Define named colour tokens (primary, surface, text, border, states) incl. dark mode if needed
Font families, sizes, weights, line heights for headings/body across breakpoints
Spacing scale, container widths, breakpoints
Buttons, links, inputs, cards, nav, modals, accordions, alerts with variants/states
Choose licensed icon set and image treatment rules
Present designs explaining rationale tied to goals
Client sends one consolidated list per round from the decision-maker
Apply agreed changes; classify out-of-scope items as change requests
Client approves designs in writing; later visual changes are change requests
Create project with chosen framework/generator, set Node version, scripts (dev/build/preview)
Folders for components, pages, styles, assets, utils; naming rules in README
Add only needed packages; commit lockfile; record licences
Common mistakes: Installing heavy libs for small needs

Description: Configure linter/formatter and optional pre-commit checks
Reset/normalize, CSS custom properties from tokens, base element styles
Implement type scale; self-host or optimise web fonts with font-display, subsetting, preload of critical font
Possible risks: Layout shift from fonts; licence breach

Description: Containers, grid/flex utilities, section spacing, responsive breakpoints
Logo, menu, active states, CTA button, skip link
Common mistakes: No active state; no skip link

Description: Accessible menu toggle (button with aria-expanded), focus management, close on Escape, scroll lock
Common mistakes: Div as button; no Escape close

Description: Contact details, links, legal pages, social links, copyright line
Implement each homepage section from design with real content
Implement each approved template and populate pages
Buttons, cards, accordions, tabs, modals, carousels (only if needed) with accessible behaviour
srcset/sizes, width/height attributes, lazy-load below fold, eager/priority for hero
Accessible fields with visible labels, autocomplete attributes, input types, required indicators
Why necessary: Forms are the main conversion point

Description: Inline validation with clear messages linked via aria-describedby; never the only validation
Button disabled/spinner on submit, skeletons for async content, prevent double submit
Friendly network/server error messages, retry, empty lists
Subtle transitions respecting prefers-reduced-motion; no layout-shifting animations
Custom 404 with navigation/search; server error page
Favicon set, apple-touch-icon, theme colour, web manifest if relevant
Central fetch/client module with timeouts, error handling, typed responses
Common mistakes: Calling third-party APIs with secret keys from browser

Description: Consent UI for non-essential cookies/trackers where client chooses to use them; blocks tags until consent
Why necessary: Privacy expectations and DPDP consent principles
Common mistakes: Banner that doesn't actually block scripts

Description: Print stylesheet for menus, price lists, event pages
Why necessary: Some local businesses need printable pages

Description: Component/unit tests for logic, basic end-to-end for key flows
Scaffold server/serverless functions with runtime version, structure, scripts
Common mistakes: Building custom backend where a service suffices

Description: .env.example with names only; secrets in host secret store; separate dev/staging/prod values
Why necessary: Secrets must never be in code or repo

Description: Implement entities (leads, bookings, products) and rules
Implement endpoints for forms, content, bookings with consistent responses
Validate type/length/format of every input; parameterised queries; encode output
Central error handler, structured logs without personal data/secrets, correlation IDs
Limit form/login/API requests per IP/user
Validate type (content not extension), size limits, virus scan if needed, private storage, random names
Why necessary: Uploads are a common attack vector

Description: Cron/scheduled tasks (reminders, cleanup, backups) with monitoring
Unit/integration tests for logic and endpoints incl. auth failures
Select managed DB appropriate to scale/budget; region; backups included
Tables/collections, relations, constraints, ERD; data minimisation
Versioned migration scripts for schema changes
Non-personal sample data for dev/staging
Add indexes for queries; unique/foreign keys
App user with only required permissions; separate admin credentials
Automated backups with retention; perform one test restore
Why necessary: Backups you haven't restored are assumptions

Description: Choose managed auth vs framework auth; define user types; passkey/OTP/password options
Why necessary: Secure login is hard to build from scratch

Description: Implement flows with secure password hashing or provider; generic error messages
Single-use, expiring tokens; rate limited; no password in email
Enforce roles/ownership on server for every protected route/object
Why necessary: Broken access control is the top web risk
Common mistakes: Hiding buttons instead of checking server-side

Description: Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite cookies; expiry; rotation on login; logout invalidation
Enable MFA/2FA on admin logins (app, platform, CMS)
Document endpoints, request/response shapes, errors, auth
Build to contract; version when breaking changes occur
Restrict keys by domain/IP/API; separate keys per environment; server-side use only for secrets
Why necessary: Stolen keys cause bills and abuse
Common mistakes: One key for dev and prod

Description: Confirm each service account is created by/for the client (client email, client billing) with you as invited user
Why necessary: Prevents developer lock-in and billing disputes

Description: Embed map or Maps API with restricted key; correct business location
Click-to-chat link with prefilled message, or Business Platform integration if requested
Common mistakes: Personal number instead of business number

Description: Links/feeds/embeds with performance and privacy consideration
Send leads/subscribers to client's CRM/list with consent recorded
Timeouts, retries, fallback (e.g., store lead locally and email) and alerts
Define fields, required ones, purpose of each, where data goes, retention
Deliver to email/DB/CRM reliably; store copy; notify client
Why necessary: Lead delivery is the site's job

Description: Honeypot, rate limit, time-trap, accessible CAPTCHA only if needed

Task: Notice and consent text on forms
Description: Short notice of purpose with link to privacy notice; separate unticked opt-in for marketing
Success message/thank-you page; fire conversion event
Submit every form on staging and production; verify email, storage, auto-reply
Why necessary: Most embarrassing failure is a silent form

Description: Configure sending service in client's account; verify sending domain
Add/merge SPF (one record), DKIM keys, DMARC policy for sending domain
Notification and auto-reply templates with plain-text version and business details
Send tests to Gmail/Outlook/Yahoo; check spam placement and headers
Set up client mailboxes on client's chosen provider; MX records
Choose CMS (none, headless, WordPress, hosted builder) based on who edits and how often
Define collections/fields/validation for editable content
Client admin, editor roles; developer account separate and removable
Enter/migrate agreed number of pages/items
Check maintenance status, security history, licence terms and renewal cost of each plugin
Why necessary: Plugins are a major vulnerability and licence risk

Description: Define admin tasks, roles, data views, exports
List/detail/edit screens with server-side authorization
Record who changed what and when for admin actions
CSV export of leads/orders for client
Why necessary: Client owns and uses their data

Description: Choose hosted platform vs WooCommerce vs custom based on SKUs, budget, maintenance, payment and GST invoicing needs
Why necessary: Custom e-commerce is expensive and risky

Description: Categories, attributes, variants, prices incl./excl. GST, images, stock
Common mistakes: Unbounded product entry in fixed fee

Description: Cart, address, shipping choice, order summary with total price, explicit consent (no pre-ticked boxes)
Why necessary: Core purchase flow; e-commerce rules require clear consent and pricing

Description: Show taxes correctly; generate GST-compliant invoices per client's CA instructions
Evidence of completion: Sample invoice reviewed by client's CA

Description: Zones, rates, delivery estimates, COD rules if offered
Display seller legal name, address, customer care and grievance officer contacts, return/refund/exchange/shipping/payment terms as supplied by client
Why necessary: Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules require prominent disclosures

Description: Customer and admin emails/SMS for order placed/shipped/refunded
Choose embedded booking service vs custom based on complexity, payments, reminders
Services, durations, buffers, staff, holidays, time zone (IST)
Email/SMS/WhatsApp confirmations, reschedule/cancel links
Two-way sync with client's calendar
Client applies and completes KYC with gateway; developer gets restricted team access
Why necessary: Settlements must go to client's bank; KYC is the merchant's obligation

Description: Use gateway's hosted page or SDK so card data never touches your server
Verify webhook signatures; confirm payment server-side; process each event once
Common mistakes: Trusting redirect URL as proof of payment

Description: Handle failures, pending, refunds and reconciliation
Swap to live keys stored as secrets; small real transaction test and refund
Short, readable, lowercase, hyphenated URLs matching IA
Unique title and description per page with brand and location where relevant
One H1 per page, logical H2/H3 nesting
Self-referencing canonicals; handle www/non-www, trailing slash, parameters
Auto-generated sitemap with production URLs only
Production robots allows crawling and lists sitemap; staging blocked/noindex + auth
LocalBusiness/Organization, breadcrumbs, FAQ/Product where accurate; validate
Common mistakes: Marking up content not on page

Description: og:title, og:description, og:image (1200×630), twitter card
Map old URLs to new with 301 redirects; test
Ensure name, address, phone match Google Business Profile and site; link website (client-owned profile)

Task: Search Console setup and sitemap submission
Description: Client verifies property (DNS preferred) as owner; developer added as user; submit sitemap
Create analytics account/property owned by client; developer as property-level user
Install analytics tag; gate on consent if client adopts consent-based approach
Track form success, calls (tel: clicks), WhatsApp clicks, bookings, purchases
Check real-time/debug data for page views and events on production
Agree target (e.g., WCAG 2.2 Level AA for templates and flows built by you) and what is out of scope (client-uploaded content)
Use header/nav/main/footer, buttons for actions, links for navigation, lists, tables correctly
All interactive elements reachable by Tab, visible focus, logical order, no traps, focus not hidden by sticky headers
Why necessary: Keyboard users and WCAG 2.2 focus criteria

Description: Meaningful alt for informative images, empty alt for decorative; captions/transcripts for video
Check text and UI component contrast in built site
Labels tied to inputs, error text announced, not colour-only, redundant entry avoided
Run automated checker on each template; fix issues
Test key flows with NVDA/VoiceOver/TalkBack: headings, landmarks, forms, menus
Set targets: LCP ≤2.5 s, INP ≤200 ms, CLS ≤0.1, page weight and JS limits
Modern formats, correct dimensions, compression, CDN
Subset, preload critical, limit weights, font-display
Remove unused code, split bundles, defer non-critical scripts, audit third-party scripts
Cache headers for static assets (hashed filenames), compression (Brotli/gzip), CDN
Lighthouse/PageSpeed on mobile profile for key templates; fix major issues
Common mistakes: Testing only desktop on fast Wi-Fi

Description: After traffic accrues, review Core Web Vitals field data (Search Console/CrUX)
Run package audit/scanner; update or replace vulnerable packages
HSTS, Content-Security-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, frame-ancestors, Permissions-Policy
Scan repo history for keys/passwords; rotate anything found
Common mistakes: Deleting file but not history/rotating key

Description: Review inputs/outputs; parameterised queries; output encoding; test common payloads
Try accessing other users' records, admin routes without auth, changing IDs
MFA, strong unique passwords, login rate limits, remove default accounts, restrict admin by role
Try disallowed types, oversized files, script files, path tricks
Debug mode off; no stack traces, versions or paths shown to users
Walk through OWASP Top 10:2025 categories relevant to the site; record status
Test on at least one mid-range Android (Chrome), one iPhone (Safari), one tablet
If skipped: Client finds bugs on own phone

Description: Targets ≥24px (aim 44px), spacing, landscape orientation, zoom not disabled
Define supported browsers/versions in scope (latest 2 versions of Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari incl. iOS)
Test key pages/flows in each matrix browser
Resolve CSS/JS compatibility issues found
Copy master QA checklist, remove non-applicable items, add project-specific flows
Test every link, button, form, navigation, search/filter, login flows per checklist
Spelling, grammar, phone numbers (tap-to-call works), emails, address, prices, hours, social links, legal pages present
Re-run key checks after fixes and before launch
Prepare staging, test script and feedback template for client acceptance testing
Log each issue with steps, expected/actual, device, severity (blocker/major/minor/cosmetic), classify bug vs change
Why necessary: Prioritises and separates defects from new requests

Description: Resolve bugs by priority with commit references
Tester (ideally other partner) verifies on staging; closes with evidence
Walk client through staging site, how to give feedback, deadline for round
One list from decision-maker per round with page, issue, screenshot
Common mistakes: Accepting WhatsApp voice notes as feedback

Description: Mark each item: bug (free), in-scope revision (counts toward round), change request (priced)
Implement in-scope revisions from round 1; send summary of changes
Final in-scope round
Tell client when included rounds are used and how further changes are billed
Record requested change: description, requester, date, reason, priority
Estimate effort, cost, timeline and risk impact; note dependencies
Client approves CR in writing (price, timeline shift); add to invoice schedule
Automated build/test/deploy from main branch to staging/prod (host-native or CI)
Set production env vars in host secret store; build with production settings
Deploy tagged release; record version, time, deployer
Documented and tested way to revert to previous release and restore DB
Domain registered by client (their registrar account, client as registrant) or client confirms existing ownership; record expiry date
Why necessary: Whoever controls the domain controls the website
Evidence of completion: WHOIS/registrar screenshot, invoice in client name
Common mistakes: Registering in developer's name 'to save time'

Description: Client enables MFA, registrar lock, auto-renew, valid recovery email/phone
Record domain, SSL (if manual), hosting, licence renewals in register and reminders
Why necessary: Renewals are the most forgotten item

Description: Export current DNS (MX, TXT, SPF, DKIM, verification, subdomains) before changes; plan new records; lower TTL 24–48 h ahead
Apply records (A/AAAA/CNAME) in client-controlled DNS
Verify from multiple resolvers; restore normal TTL; remove obsolete records
Common mistakes: Leaving old CNAMEs to deleted services

Description: Choose host by stack, traffic, region, backups, support, cost, renewal price
Client creates account and billing; developer invited as member/collaborator
For VPS: OS updates, firewall, SSH keys only, no root login, fail2ban/equivalent, automatic security updates
Issue certificate (host-managed or ACME) for apex and www; confirm auto-renew
Why necessary: HTTPS required by browsers and users

Description: 301 HTTP→HTTPS and non-canonical host (www or apex) to canonical; HSTS when stable
Ensure all assets load over HTTPS
Debug off, correct env, logging level, error pages, timezone, email sender
Buckets private by default; public only for public assets; signed URLs for private files
Monitor homepage and key endpoint; alerts to client and/or maintainer
Common mistakes: Alerts only to developer after handover

Description: Capture frontend/backend errors with PII scrubbing
Complete launch checklist (SEO, forms, analytics, legal pages, redirects, backups, robots)
Client gives written final approval; agree go-live date/time (avoid Friday evening, festivals)
Execute deploy + DNS cutover per plan; monitor
Ensure staging remains password-protected/noindexed or is taken down
Draft announcement post/email/WhatsApp status for client
Test key pages, navigation, mobile view, HTTPS on live domain

Task: Live forms, emails and payments test
Description: Real submissions and (if applicable) small live payment + refund on production
Submit sitemap, inspect homepage URL in Search Console, confirm no noindex
Review errors, uptime, analytics, form deliveries, Search Console coverage over first 7–14 days
Assemble docs, account register, licence register, design files, source code access, backups, maintenance options
Walk through site, accounts, how to get help, what warranty covers, renewals
Client signs acknowledgement listing items received and access confirmed
Setup, build, deploy steps, env var names (not values), architecture, dependencies, known issues
Common mistakes: Writing it at the last minute

Description: How to edit content, add images, manage forms/leads, common tasks with screenshots
Every account/service: owner, URL, purpose, who has access, renewal date, cost, where credentials are stored (not the credentials)
List fonts, images, icons, themes, plugins, libraries with licence type, licensee, proof, renewal
Live training on content edits and admin tasks; record with consent
Answer follow-up questions within agreed window
Invoice remaining balance plus approved change orders, less advance
Confirm bank credit, issue receipt, update ledger
Request TDS certificate for amounts deducted; reconcile with AIS/26AS
Confirm client is registrant and sole account holder; developer removed from registrar; if transfer needed, initiate with auth code (TAC/EPP) securely
Transfer project/team ownership or confirm client-owned account; downgrade/remove developer access
Transfer repo to client org/account or deliver full archive; confirm client admin; remove developer collaborator if not maintaining
Confirm client is GA Administrator and verified Search Console owner; remove developer tokens/access or downgrade
Common mistakes: Removing user but not verification token

Description: For each service in register: confirm client owner, billing, API key ownership; transfer anything created by developer
